content.title: About
content.content: Meat pizza on a gluten‑free thick crust is a tasty twist on the classic pie, made with a special gluten‑free dough, tomato sauce, aromatic herbs, and a generous layer of meat toppings such as ham, sausage, and beef.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free dough allows people with celiac disease to enjoy pizza safely.
A thick crust retains the moisture of the toppings and gives a richer flavor.
Meat blends often combine several types of meat for a more complex taste profile.
Traditional pizza is baked at 250‑300 °C (475‑570 °F) to achieve a crisp crust.
Gluten‑free pizzas have become popular among athletes and low‑carb diet followers.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and tomato sauce deliver vitamins B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: The dough is suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten‑sensitivity.

items.title: Provides fiber
items.content: If the dough includes whole‑grain or seed additives, the pizza can contribute modest dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A thick crust and meat toppings make the pizza calorie‑dense, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat and cheese can contain saturated fats, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats like sausage and ham are often high in salt, a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some gluten‑free flour blends may contain soy or nuts, which can trigger allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into portions and serve hot. You can add fresh vegetables, basil, or a light green salad dressing to balance the flavors.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.
